svg.aria-label: Why ECB mode leaks patterns, and how AES-GCM fixes it, using the Week 3 lab example. The plaintext is two identical sixteen-byte blocks, both the letter A repeated sixteen times. Under ECB mode each block is encrypted independently with the same key, so the two identical plaintext blocks produce two identical ciphertext blocks — the same hex bytes repeat, so the repetition in the data is still visible in the ciphertext. This is the classic ECB-penguin effect: the shape survives encryption. Encrypting the exact same two-block input again gives the exact same ciphertext, because there is no nonce. Under AES-GCM the same plaintext produces two different, random-looking ciphertext blocks, plus a random nonce and an authentication tag, so no pattern is visible and any tampering is detected. Bottom line: ECB encrypts each block independently, so identical plaintext yields identical ciphertext and patterns leak; AES-GCM with a random nonce gives confidentiality and integrity together. Choosing AES is not enough — AES in ECB mode, or AES-GCM under a hardcoded key, is still broken.
svg.title: Why ECB leaks — identical plaintext blocks become identical ciphertext blocks, and how AES-GCM fixes it (Week 3, CWE-327)
svg.text: Why ECB leaks — identical blocks become identical ciphertext
Week 3 · AES misuse · CWE-327 · encrypt_ecb(b"A"*16 + b"A"*16) in vulnerable_crypto.py
ECB — each block encrypted independently, same key, no nonce
→ the repeat is still visible (the "ECB penguin")
Encrypt the same input again → the exact same bytes. Patterns — and equality — leak straight through.
→ no visible pattern · tampering is detected
nonce (os.urandom) makes each encryption unique; the tag proves the ciphertext wasn't altered.
ECB reuses no state between blocks, so equal plaintext → equal ciphertext. AES-GCM adds a random nonce
(confidentiality) and an auth tag (integrity). Choosing AES is not the fix — AES-ECB leaks, and AES-GCM under a
hardcoded key is still CWE-798. fix: solution_skeleton.py encrypt_gcm() — GCM + random nonce + key from env.
